source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: Having heard that Ushanas was angry, the distressed son of Nahusha, Yayati, then, having immediately obtained extreme old age, spoke these words to Yadu.
verses.2: Yayati said, "O Yadu, you are a knower of righteousness; for my sake, please accept this extreme old age, O son, so that I, O greatly renowned one, may delight in enjoyments."
verses.3: Yayati continued, "O best among men, I am not yet satisfied with worldly pleasures; only after fully experiencing my desires will I then accept old age."
verses.4: Having heard those words, Yadu replied to his father, the best among men, saying, "Let your beloved son Puru indeed accept this old age."
verses.5: O King, I am excluded from worldly pleasures due to old age; who indeed would eat food with me?
verses.6: Having heard his words, the king then spoke to Puru, saying, "O mighty-armed one, let this old age be accepted for my sake."
verses.7: Thus addressed by Yayati, Puru spoke with folded hands, saying, "I am blessed, I am favored, and I abide by your command."
verses.8: Having understood Puru's words, Yayati obtained unequalled delight with great joy and transferred that old age to him.
verses.9: Thereafter, that king, having become young again, performed thousands of sacrifices and ruled the earth for many thousands of years.
verses.10: After a long time, King Yayati then spoke to Puru, saying, "O son, bring back my old age; return the deposit to me."
verses.11: O son, that old age was transferred to you by me as a deposit; therefore, I will take it back, so do not feel distressed.
verses.12: O mighty-armed one, I am pleased by your acceptance of my command, and I will affectionately anoint you as the king of men.
verses.13: Having thus spoken to his son Puru, King Yayati, the son of Nahusha, then spoke enraged words to Devayani's son.
verses.14: You are a wicked demon born by me in the form of a son, because you reject my command, you shall become fruitless in terms of progeny.
verses.15: Because you disrespect me, your father and preceptor, you will give birth to terrible Rakshasas and Yatudhanas.
verses.16: The lineage of that evil-minded one (Yati) will not endure in the Lunar dynasty, and your own progeny will also be ill-behaved like you.
verses.17: Having thus spoken, the royal sage Yayati honored Puru, who was destined to expand the kingdom, with a coronation and then entered his hermitage.
verses.18: After a long time, King Yayati, the son of Nahusha, reached the end of his life and ascended to heaven.
verses.19: The greatly renowned Puru, endowed with great righteousness, ruled that kingdom from the excellent city of Pratishthana in the Kashi region.
verses.20: King Yadu, having been excluded from the royal lineage, begot thousands of Rākṣasas in the inaccessible region of Krauñcavana.
verses.21: This curse, given by Uśanas, was indeed borne by Yayāti due to his Kṣatriya duty, a burden which even Nimi could not tolerate.
verses.22: O gentle one, all this has been narrated to you as a lesson for all actions, so that we may follow it and avoid a fault like that of Nṛga.
verses.23: As Rāma, whose face was like the moon, spoke thus, the sky at that time became very sparse with stars, and the eastern direction shone, reddened by the rays of dawn, like a faded garment being rolled up. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 59 ।। Thus ends the fifty-ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
